ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r3.claim: Pharaoh's exemplary punishment included drowning in this world and consigning him to Hell in the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r3.anchor: the Almighty seized him in the punishment of this world and that of the next

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r1.claim: نكال is an accusative verbal noun; interpreters disagree about which of Pharaoh's two boasts is the former and which is the latter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r1.anchor: نكال منصوب على المصدر، قال قوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r2.claim: A report says Pharaoh lived forty years after claiming to be the highest lord; another makes this the interval between his two statements.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r2.anchor: وروي أنه مكث بعد قوله: أنا ربكم الأعلى [النازعات: 24] أربعين سنة، وقيل هذه المدة بين الكلمتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reverses that identification: the denial of any other god came first and the highest-lord claim came last.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الأولى قوله: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r4.claim: Abu Zayd says the former means Pharaoh's disbelief and disobedience, while the latter is his highest-lord claim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: الأولى كفره وعصيانه، والآخرة قوله: أنا ربكم الأعلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the former and latter as this world and the afterlife: drowning was his worldly punishment and Hell his final one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الأولى الدنيا، والآخرة: الدار الآخرة، أي أخذه الله بعذاب جهنم وبالغرق في الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r6.claim: Mujahid interprets the former and latter as Pharaoh's first and last acts of disobedience and disbelief; God punished all of them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عبارة عن أول معاصيه وكفره وآخرها أي نكل بالجميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r7.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r7.claim: Sibawayh says the verbal noun is governed by أخذ because it carries that meaning; al-Mubarrad instead supplies an implicit verb from نكال.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r7.anchor: والعامل فيه على رأي سيبويه «أخذ» لأنه في معناه، وعلى رأي أبي العباس المبرد فعل مضمر

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r27.claim: Nekāl is a verbal noun for deterrent punishment: it chastises as an example and prevents others from repeating the causes of the offense.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r27.anchor: “Nekâl” de tenkil mânasına ism-i masdar olur. “Tenkîl” gören ve işitene ibret olacak ve ona müeddî olan şeylerden men‘edecek vechile ta‘zîb ve ukūbet etmektir.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r28.claim: He parses nekāl either as an absolute object with the clause circumstantial, or as the reason for God seizing Pharaoh.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r28.anchor: Burada “nekâl” نَكَلَهُ اللهُ نَكَالَ الاْٰخِرَةِ وَالاُْولٰى takdîrinde mef‘ûl-i mutlak, cümlesi hâl mevkiindedir. Veya

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r29.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r29.claim: On the apparent reading, the first and hereafter punishments mean drowning in this world and consignment to Hell in the next.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r29.anchor: Âhiret ve ûlâdan zâhir olan âhiret ve dünyadır ki dünya nekâli iğrâk ile, âhiret nekâli cehenneme sevk ile olmuştur.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r30.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r30.claim: Ibn Jarīr also reads “later” and “former” as Pharaoh's two statements: “I am your highest lord” and “I know no god for you but me.”
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r30.anchor: “sonraki”nden murad أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ kelimesi, “evvelki”nden murad da مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى [el-Kasas 28/38] kelimesi demek olduğu da İbn Cerîr tefsirinde mezkurdur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r14.claim: The author translates verse 25 as God giving Pharaoh exemplary punishment in this world and the next.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r14.anchor: “Allah da ona ibretlik dünya ve âhiret cezası verdi” diye çevirdiğimiz 25. âyete

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r15.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r15.claim: Qurṭubī offers the alternative reading that God punished Pharaoh for both his later and earlier statements.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r15.anchor: “Allah da onu hem sonraki sözünden hem de önceki sözünden dolayı cezalandırdı” şeklinde de mâna verilmiştir

QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s punishment is a lesson for the one who fears: the soul should humble, soften, and break so it no longer makes claims.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.anchor: ويروى: قصمته، وذلك القهر هو معنى قوله: { فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى * إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى }

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r5.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say God made Pharaoh a warning by drowning him in this life and condemning him to the Fire in the next.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r5.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: عاقبه الله فجعله نكال الآخرة والأولى، أي في الدنيا بالغرق وفي الآخرة بالنار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r6.speaker: مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r6.claim: Mujāhid and a group of commentators take the first and later events as Pharaoh's two boasts, in 28:38 and 79:24, spoken forty years apart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين: أراد بالآخرة والأولى كلمتي فرعون قوله: "ما علمت لكم من إله غيري"

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r3.claim: God's punishment was a retribution for later and earlier deeds: burning in the Hereafter and drowning in this world.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r3.anchor: { فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى } أخذا منكلا لمن رآه، أو سمعه في الآخرة بالإحراق وفي الدنيا بالإغراق

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r4.claim: Alternatively, the later deed is the boast in this passage and the earlier one is Pharaoh's claim in 28:38.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r4.anchor: أو على كلمته { الآخرة } وهي هذه وكلمته الأولى وهو قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r5.claim: Alternatively, the punishment is retribution for both the later and earlier deeds.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r6.claim: Grammatically, نكالا may be an emphatic cognate accusative with an implied verb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا مؤكدا مقدرا بفعله

BINTSHATI:v1p148/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r3.claim: Nikl first means an animal’s restraint or bridle, then by extension denotes humiliation, from the degradation of someone fettered.
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r3.anchor: أصل النكل في اللغة: قيد الدابة وحديدة اللجام. نكلته: قيدته. لحظ فيه عجز المنكول وهوانه، فاستعمل التنكيل في مطلق الإذلال،

BINTSHATI:v1p148/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r4.claim: The Qur’anic root appears in five places: as ankāl in al-Muzzammil, tankīl in al-Nisāʾ, and nikāl in al-Baqara, al-Māʾida, and al-Naziʿat.
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r4.anchor: وجاءت المادة في القرآن في خمسة مواضع: المزمل 12: {إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا}

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r1.claim: The punishment in al-Naziʿat is that of Moses’ Pharaoh.

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r2.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r2.claim: One interpretation is that Pharaoh was drowned in this life and burned in the afterlife.
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r2.anchor: أحدهما، إنه الإغراق في الدنيا والإحراق في الآخرة.

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r3.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r3.claim: A second interpretation takes “the last and the first” as Pharaoh’s two blasphemous claims, including “I am your highest lord” and “I know no god but me.”
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه نكال كلمتيه الآخرة وألولى فقد قال مرة: {أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى} . وقال أخرى: {مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي} (القصص 38) .

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r4.claim: The context gives no sign that the phrases mean Pharaoh’s two statements, so the author prefers “the afterlife and the first” as the two lives, here and hereafter.
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r4.anchor: وليس في السياق هنا ما يشير إلى احتمال أن يقصد بالأخرى والأولى في النازعات كلمتان لفرعون، وإنما نطمئن فيها إلى تفسير الآخرة والأولى، بالحياتين الأخرى والدنيا.

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r5.claim: The afterlife is mentioned first because its punishment is more severe and lasting.
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r5.anchor: وقدمت الآخرة على الأولى، لآن نكالها أفدح وأبقى.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r13.claim: Pharaoh was seized with punishment in both the afterlife and the first life; the passage links this to his drowning and the curse on his followers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r13.anchor: فإنها مصرحة بوقوع نكاله في الآخرة كما وقع في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r14.claim: The author says God did not explicitly condemn anyone or declare anyone's wretchedness as forcefully as in Pharaoh's case.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r14.anchor: هذا الذي لم يصرح الله بذم أحد ما صرح بذمه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r7.claim: God seized Pharaoh with humiliating overpowering force as the sole sovereign beside whom no equal or other command exists.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r7.anchor: { فأخذه الله } أي الملك الذي لا كفوء له ولا أمر لأحد معه أخذ قهر وذل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r8.claim: The afterlife punishment is an exemplary deterrent, making hearers wary of imitating Pharaoh.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r8.anchor: { نكال الآخرة } فهو مصدر من المعنى , أي أخذ تنكيل فيها يكون مثلا يتقيد به ويتعظ كل من سمعه عن مثل حال فرعون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r9.claim: The afterlife punishment is foregrounded because it is greater and more severe; this order is for emphasis, not rhyme, since ‘the other’ would rhyme with ‘the first.’
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r9.anchor: وليس ذلك للفاصلة لأنه لو قيل : ( الأخرى ) لوافقت { والأولى * }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r10.claim: Pharaoh’s worldly fate also serves as a deterrent against repeating his conduct or anything lesser.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r10.anchor: كان له ذلك نكالا مانعا من عمل مثله أو أقل منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r11.speaker: الضحاك
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Pharaoh was drowned and cast ashore in this world, then will be exposed atop the Fire in chains, proclaimed as the claimant to lordship besides God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r11.anchor: قال الضحاك : أما في الدنيا فأغرقه الله تعالى وألقاء بنجوة من الأرض , أما في العقبى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r12.claim: Al-Biqāʿī condemns al-Ḥallāj, Ibn ʿArabī, Ibn al-Fāriḍ, and their followers as destined for the Fire for endorsing and repeating Pharaoh’s claim against the Qurʾān.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r12.anchor: وأنا لا أشك أن الحلاج وابن عربي وابن الفارض , وأتباعهم يكونون في النار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r13.claim: He charges them with abusing the Greatest Name by claiming it applies to themselves, everyone, and everything, after God had protected it from such claims before the Prophet’s mission.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r13.anchor: وزادوا عليه بابتذال الاسم الأعظم الذي حماه الله من أن يدعيه أحد قبل إرسال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فادعوا أنه يطلق عليهم وعلى كل أحد بل كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r8.claim: “Seizing” literally means taking by hand but often figuratively means power and triumph; Pharaoh could not escape God’s punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r8.anchor: وحقيقة الأخذ : التناول باليد ، ويستعار كثيرا للمقدرة والغلبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r9.claim: Nakal is a verbal noun like salām; it means inflicting severe, public humiliation so witnesses are deterred from repeating the offense, from a root meaning retreat or flight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r9.anchor: ومعنى النكال : إيقاع أذى شديد على الغير من التشهير بذلك بحيث ينكل ، أي يرد ويصرف من يشاهده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r4.claim: God exacted vengeance on Pharaoh, making him a warning and deterrent for rebellious people in this world.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r4.anchor: انتقم الله منه انتقاما جعله به عبرة ونكالا لأمثاله من المتمردين في الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says “the former and latter punishment” means this world and the Hereafter, calling this the correct interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r5.anchor: هذا هو الصحيح في معنى الآية، أن المراد بقوله: {نكال الآخرة والأولى} أي: الدنيا والآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r6.claim: One reported interpretation takes the phrase to refer to Pharaoh’s first and second statements.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: المراد بذلك كلمتاه الأولى والثانية. وقيل: كفره وعصيانه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r7.claim: Another reported interpretation takes it to mean Pharaoh’s disbelief and disobedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: كفره وعصيانه. والصحيح الذي لا شك فيه الأول

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r11.claim: Nakal is a deterrent punishment, named from prevention; shackles restrain, and the punishment prevents repeating its cause, while related forms also mean refraining or preventing someone.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r11.anchor: والنكال: العقوبة التي تنكل الناس عن فعل ما جعلت له جزاء، وأصله: المنع، ومنه سمي القيد نكلا

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Pharaoh was punished in this world by drowning and in the Hereafter by fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r1.anchor: بالنار، عن الحسن، وقتادة، وقيل: نكال كلمته الأولى والأخرى

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد والشعبي، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Shaʿbi, and Qatada identify the two punishments with Pharaoh's first claim, that he knew no god for them but himself, and his last claim, that he was their highest lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r2.anchor: وقيل: نكال كلمته الأولى والأخرى، فالأولى قوله: (ما علمت لكم من إله غيري) والأحرى قوله: (أنا ربكم الأعلى)، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد والشعبي، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r3.claim: An unattributed report says forty years separated Pharaoh's first and last claims.

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r8.claim: Punishment in one of the two abodes does not rule out punishment in the other.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (نكال الآخرة والأولى) أن عقوبة إحدى الدارين لا تمنع عقوبة الدار الأخرى

MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God seized Pharaoh for both claims: first that he knew no god for his people except himself, then that he was their highest lord.
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ﴿ فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى ﴾ يقول أخذه الله بكلمتيه كلتيهما أما كلمته الأولى قوله ﴿ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ﴾ وأما الآخرة

MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation as Ibn Abbas for Pharaoh's punishment for his two claims.
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد مثله

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r15.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r15.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r15.claim: Forty years separated Pharaoh's earlier claim to be the only god and his later claim to be the highest lord.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r15.anchor: وكان بينهما أربعين سنة، الأولى قوله:

NAHHAS:v5p143/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r15.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p143/r15.claim: He says God seized Pharaoh with a punitive seizure for the earlier and later transgressions.
NAHHAS:v5p143/r15.anchor: قال الفراء أي فأخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r14.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r14.claim: They identify the first and later exemplary punishments with Pharaoh's claim to be the only deity in 28:38 and his later boast that he was the highest lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r14.anchor: «أنا ربكم الأعلى» قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r15.claim: He says forty years separated Pharaoh's two blasphemous statements.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r15.anchor: وكان بين الكلمتين أربعون سنة قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r16.claim: God delayed punishment after the first statement, then seized and punished Pharaoh for both statements later.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r16.anchor: والمعنى: أمهله في الأولى، ثم أخذه في الآخرة، فعذبه بكلمتيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r17.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r17.claim: An alternative identifies the first punishment as drowning and the later one as punishment in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r17.anchor: وقيل: نكال الأولى: هو أن أغرقه، ونكال الآخرة: العذاب في الآخرة. وقاله قتادة وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r18.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r18.claim: He interprets the two punishments as affliction at the beginning and end of Pharaoh's life.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r18.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو عذاب أول عمره وآخره.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r19.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r19.claim: Another report from him assigns the later punishment to Pharaoh's highest-lord claim and the first to his denial of Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r19.anchor: وقيل: الآخرة قوله «أنا ربكم الأعلى» والأولى تكذيبه لموسى. عن قتادة أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r20.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r20.claim: He parses nikal as an emphatic cognate accusative: the phrase means God punished him, with nikal replacing a synonymous verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r20.anchor: و «نكال» منصوب على المصدر المؤكد في قول الزجاج لأن معنى أخذه الله: نكل الله به

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r21.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r21.claim: Another grammatical explanation makes nikal accusative after an omitted preposition, as if the phrase said God seized him with exemplary punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r21.anchor: وقيل: نصب بنزع حرف الصفة، أي فأخذه الله بنكال الآخرة، فلما نزع الخافض نصب.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r22.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r22.claim: Al-Farra reads the phrase as God seized him with a seizure serving as a deterrent.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r22.anchor: وقال الفراء: أي أخذه الله أخذا نكالا، أي للنكال.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r23.claim: Nikal is a deterrent punishment imposed so others take warning; nakala means to punish severely, while related words mean abstaining from an oath and a fetter.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r23.anchor: والنكال: اسم لما جعل نكالا للغير أي عقوبة له حتى يعتبر به.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r24.claim: The discussion of nikal was already given in Surat al-Muzzammil.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r24.anchor: وقد مضى في سورة «المزمل» والحمد لله.

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r6.claim: After recounting Pharaoh's deeds and words, Razi says the text next recounts how God dealt with him: He seized him as a lesson for the latter and former generations.
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r6.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى عنه أفعاله وأقواله أتبعه بما عامله به

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r1.claim: This is probably the earliest-revealed Quranic account of Moses; it assumes Arabs knew the story and warns the Prophet and his followers about the fate of unjust rulers such as Makkah's rulers.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r1.anchor: This is most likely the first account of Moses in the chronological order of revelation. As it occurred early in the Makkan period

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r17.claim: Nakāl also connotes weakness and inability, suggesting God rendered Pharaoh powerless to oppose Moses.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r17.anchor: nakāl, which also indicates weakness and inability, evoking the sense that God rendered Pharaoh impotent in opposing Moses.

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r18.claim: The verse describes punishment in this world and the next; its worldly punishment is commonly taken as the plagues and Pharaoh's drowning with his people.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r18.anchor: many interpret the this-worldly punishment as the plagues sent upon his people and their drowning in the sea

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r19.speaker: Q, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r19.claim: A variant reading calls the punishment “of the last and the first.”
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r19.anchor: Some read this verse as “the punishment of the last and the first,”

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r20.speaker: Q, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r20.claim: Under one explanation of that reading, the first punishment answers Pharaoh's claim to know no god but himself, and the last answers his claim to be the highest lord.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r20.anchor: “the first”indicates the punishment for saying, I know of no god for you other than myself

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r21.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r21.claim: Another explanation assigns the first punishment to Pharaoh's denial of Moses and the last to his claim to be the highest lord.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r21.anchor: others say“the first” is for denying Moses and “the last” is for saying, I am your lord most high (Q).

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r22.claim: A Sufi account attributed to al-Simnānī contrasts Pharaoh, who saw only himself and forgot God, with al-Ḥallāj, who saw only God and forgot himself.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r22.anchor: In a well-known Sufi interpretation, Alāʾ al-Dawlā al-Simnānī (d. 787/1336) is said to have seen the soul

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r8.claim: God's taking Pharaoh is a figure for punishing him; nakal is deterrent punishment, and both worldly destruction and afterlife punishment deter others.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r8.anchor: الأخذ كناية عن التعذيب، والنكال التعذيب الذي يردع من رآه أو سمعه عن تعاطي مثله

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r9.claim: The former and latter refer to this world and the Hereafter: Pharaoh and his troops drowned here, and he faces punishment after death.

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r10.claim: One view takes the latter as Pharaoh's final boast and the former as his earlier claim that he knew no god besides himself, making both utterances the cause of his punishment.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r10.anchor: وقيل المراد بالآخرة كلمته الآخرة، { أنا ربكم الأعلى } وبالأولى كلمته الأولى قالها قبل ذلك

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r11.claim: The interpretation that the two terms designate Pharaoh's two statements is obscure.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r11.anchor: ولا يخلو هذا المعنى من خفاء

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r12.claim: Another reading takes the first as Pharaoh's denial and disobedience at the beginning of the story and the latter as his final boast.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد بالأولى تكذيبه ومعصيته المذكوران في أول القصة وبالأخرى كلمة - أنا ربكم الأعلى - المذكورة في آخرها

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r13.claim: The reading that the terms refer to the beginning and ending of the story is likewise obscure.

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r14.claim: A further view means the first and last of Pharaoh's sins, so God punished him for their totality.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r14.anchor: وقيل الاولى أول معاصيه والأخرى آخرها والمعنى أخذه الله نكال مجموع معاصيه

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r15.claim: The interpretation that the two terms mean the first and last of all his sins is also obscure.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r6.claim: God punished Pharaoh as an example: with Hell in the next life and drowning in this life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r6.anchor: فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى } أي: نكل الله به في الآخرة بالعذاب في النار، وفي الدنيا بالغرق.

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats nakālan as an emphatic cognate accusative: taking Pharaoh means God made an exemplary punishment of him, like saying I leave him a severe leaving.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r1.anchor: إنه مصدر مؤكد لأن معنى أخذه الله ، نكل الله به

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an understood noun: God seized him with a seizure serving as a warning; nakāl means tankīl, like salām for taslīm.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r2.anchor: يريد أخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى ، والنكال بمعنى التنكيل

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r3.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل، وعطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r3.claim: The two descriptions are Pharaoh's claims to divinity in 28:38 and 79:24; he was spared forty years after the first, then seized for both.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r3.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل ، ورواية عطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read the punishment as torment in the hereafter and drowning in this world.

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r5.claim: Al-Qaffāl identifies the later offense as Pharaoh's final boast and the earlier one as rejecting Moses after the sign; Rāzī calls this the clearest reading because the passage names these two offenses in sequence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r5.anchor: قال القفال : وهذا كأنه هو الأظهر ، لأنه تعالى قال

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r6.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r6.claim: Al-Layth defines nakāl as an exemplary warning; its root carries prevention, as in refusing an oath or a restraining fetter.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r6.anchor: قال الليث : ( النكال ) اسم لمن جعل نكالا لعيره

RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r7.claim: In ordinary usage the punishment is a disgraceful spectacle that makes others refrain from repeating the offender's sin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40/r7.anchor: فالنكال من العقوبة هو أعظم حتى يمتنع من سمع به عن ارتكاب مثل ذلك الذنب

TAB-FULL:v24p87/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r1.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r1.claim: Abū Razīn says the earlier punishment was Pharaoh’s denial and disobedience, while the later was his claim “I am your highest lord.”
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r1.anchor: عن أبي رزين، {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى} [النازعات: 25] قال: الأولى تكذيبه وعصيانه

TAB-FULL:v24p87/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r2.claim: Mujāhid says God’s punishment encompassed Pharaoh’s first and last deeds.
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى} [النازعات: 25] قال: أول عمله وآخره

TAB-FULL:v24p87/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r3.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī describes the punishment of the later act as being for disobedience and the earlier act.
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r3.anchor: عن الكلبي، {أخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى} قال: نكال الآخرة من المعصية والأولى

TAB-FULL:v24p87/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r4.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the phrase as Pharaoh’s deed for the afterlife and the earlier life.
TAB-FULL:v24p87/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {نكال الآخرة والأولى} [النازعات: 25] قال: عمله للآخرة والأولى

TABRISI:79:25-26/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r1.claim: Pharaoh was seized and made an example of: God drowned him in this world and will punish him in the next.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r1.anchor: بأن أغرقه في الدنيا ويعذبه في الآخرة

TABRISI:79:25-26/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r2.claim: An alternative reads the punishment as retribution for Pharaoh’s final claim, “I am your highest lord,” and earlier claim that he knew no god but himself.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه فعاقبه الله بكلمته الآخرة وكلمته الأولى

TABRISI:79:25-26/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:79:25-26/r3.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says forty years separated Pharaoh’s two statements.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير عن أبي جعفر ع أنه كان بين الكلمتين أربعون سنة

TABRISI:79:25-26/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r4.claim: Another account says Pharaoh invoked his claim to divinity while asking his people to protect him from a snake; fearing harm and seeking help disproves divinity.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r4.anchor: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى فامنعوني من هذا الثعبان ولم يعلم الجهال

TABRISI:79:25-26/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:79:25-26/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Moses asking why Pharaoh was spared for four hundred years despite blasphemy; God answers that Pharaoh was courteous and hospitable, so God repaid him for that.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r5.anchor: عن وهب عن ابن عباس قال قال موسى ع

TABRISI:79:25-26/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r6.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:79:25-26/r6.claim: A report through Abu Jaʿfar quotes the Prophet recounting Gabriel’s question about Pharaoh; God says only one afraid of missing out makes such a claim.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r6.anchor: روى أبو بصير عن أبي جعفر ع قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال جبرائيل ع

TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.claim: The account of Moses follows mention of those who denied prophets and resurrection, consoling Muhammad, urging patience after Moses, warning his people, and reinforcing the proof.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.anchor: وجه اتصال قصة موسى ع بما قبلها أنه لما تقدم ذكر المكذبين للأنبياء المنكرين للبعث

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r1.claim: Among creatures, the human being claims the greatest perfection: Pharaoh claimed lordship, while Iblīs disclaimed it and never claimed a station he did not possess; Iblīs has only majesty, angels pure beauty, and humans both, being created with two hands.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : لم يدع أحد من الخلائق من الكمال ما ادعاه ادعاه الإنسان

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r2.speaker: ركن الدين علاء الدولة السمناني
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r2.claim: Al-Sumnānī recounts visiting al-Ḥallāj’s spirit in a spiritual state and asking why Pharaoh’s “I am your highest lord” and al-Ḥallāj’s “I am the Real” led to opposite fates; the answer is that Pharaoh saw only himself and diminished God, while al-Ḥallāj saw God and diminished himself.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r2.anchor: شيخ ركن الدين علاء الدولة سمناني قدس سره فرموده كه وقتى مرا حال كرم بود

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r3.speaker: مولانا
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r3.claim: Rūmī’s verses distinguish Pharaoh’s “I am the Real,” which brings curse, from al-Ḥallāj’s, which brings mercy: Pharaoh’s I is stone and an enemy of light, while al-Ḥallāj’s is precious stone and a lover; theirs is arrogance, not union or incarnation.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r3.anchor: وفي المثنوى) : كفت فرعوني أنا الحق كشت ست

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r4.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r4.claim: One answer to why Iblīs was singled out for a curse while Pharaoh was not is that Iblīs’ intention was worse than theirs.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r4.anchor: قال في أسئلة الحكم فإن قلت ما الحكمة في إن إبليس قد لعن ولم يدع الربوبية

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r5.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r5.claim: A second answer is that Iblīs was first in initiating disobedience and discord in word, deed, and intention; later claims of lordship and oppression arose through his whispering.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r5.anchor: وقيل لأنه أول من سن الخلاف والشقاق قولا وفعلا ونية

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r6.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r6.claim: Iblīs confronted God directly in disobedience, while Pharaoh and others confronted prophets and intermediaries and sometimes confessed sins or supplicated to creatures; Iblīs neither confessed nor humbled himself.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r6.anchor: وإبليس واجه بمخالفته حضرة الرب تعالى وهم واجهوا الأنبياء والوسائط

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r7.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r7.claim: Iblīs was the first to institute disbelief and the direct source of misguidance, so the burden of disbelievers who follow returns to him until the Day of Judgment.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r7.anchor: فوزر الكفار بعده راجع إليه إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r8.claim: نكال means deterrent punishment that prevents anyone who sees or hears of it from attempting what leads to such a fate.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r8.anchor: الذي ينكل من رأه أو سمعه ويمعنه من تعاطي ما يفضي إليه

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r9.claim: نكال is used as a verbal noun of تنكيل, like سلام for تسليم, and is accusative as an emphatic cognate object.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r9.anchor: النكال بمعنى التنكيل كالسلام بمعنى التسليم وهو التعذيب

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r10.claim: God’s punishment was drowning in this world and burning in the next; the phrase refers to both punishments.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r10.anchor: وهو الإحراق في الآخرة والإغراق في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r11.claim: أخذ extends figuratively across worldly and afterlife punishment, since the worldly taking is literal and the afterlife taking figurative; the two abodes are named because the punishment occurs in both.
BURSEVI:v10p250#2/r11.anchor: وإضافة النكال إلى الدارين باعتبار وقوع نفس الأخذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق، المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq treats nakāl as an emphatic verbal noun: taking Pharaoh means punishing him; al-Mubarrad agrees, as in 11:102.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r2.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases it as God seizing him with exemplary punishment for this life and the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: يريد أخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r3.speaker: مجاهد، الشعبي، سعيد بن جبير، مقاتل، عطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r3.claim: One view takes the two terms as Pharaoh’s claims, “I know no god for you but me” and later “I am your highest lord,” forty years apart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r3.anchor: وهذا قول (مجاهد (¬2)، والشعبي (¬3)، وسعيد بن جبير (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r4.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p189/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Pharaoh was drowned and punished in this world, then punished in the afterlife.

BURHAN:v3p263/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p263/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p263/r3.claim: The reversed order الآخرة والأولى is chosen to match the verse endings, as in the parallel phrase فلله الآخرة والأولى.

SULAMI:v2p371/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371/r1.speaker: بشر
SULAMI:v2p371/r1.claim: God made Pharaoh’s tongue speak allusively of claims of lordship while emptying those claims of any reality.
SULAMI:v2p371/r1.anchor: قال بشر في هذه الآية : انطق الله لسانه بالتعريض من الدعاوي واخلاه من حقائقها

SULAMI:v2p371/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371/r2.speaker: سري
SULAMI:v2p371/r2.claim: A servant who assumes a master’s guise becomes an example of punishment: after Pharaoh claimed lordship, God chastised him in both worlds and everything, even Pharaoh himself, refuted the claim.
SULAMI:v2p371/r2.anchor: وقال سرى - رحمة الله عليه - : العبد إذا تزيا بزي السيد صار نكالا

FARRA:v3p232/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r1.claim: The two utterances are فرعون's claims that he knows no god for his people but himself and that he is their highest lord; God seized him as a chastisement for both.
FARRA:v3p232/r1.anchor: إحدى الكلمتين قوله: «ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#4/r1.claim: The “later” statement was Pharaoh’s claim “I am your lord most high” (79:24), and the “first” was “I know no god for you other than myself” (28:38).
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#4/r1.anchor: فإحداهما قوله: {أنا ربكم الأعلى [24] } ؛ والأخرى قوله: {ما علمت لكم من إله غيري} (4) .

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r1.claim: نكال may be a verbal noun of أخذ, with figurative usage either in the verb (he punished him by taking) or in the noun (he took him as a punishment).
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مصدرا ل " أخذ " ، والتجوز: إما في الفعل، أي: نكل بالأخذ نكال الآخرة، وإما في المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r2.claim: Alternatively, نكال is a purpose object: God seized him in order to punish him as a warning.
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا له، أي: لأجل نكاله

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r3.claim: Taking نكال as a circumstantial accusative is weak because it is definite and requires an unmeasured interpretation like جهدك and طاقتك.
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r3.anchor: ويضعف جعله حالا لتعريفه، وتأويله كتأويل جهدك وطاقتك غير مقيس

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes نكال as an emphatic verbal noun for the preceding clause, like وعد الله and صبغة الله.
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا مؤكدا لمضمون الجملة المتقدمة، أي: نكل الله به نكال الآخرة، قاله الزمخشري، وجعله ك وعد الله

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r5.claim: نكال has the sense of تنكيل, just as سلام can mean تسليم.
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r5.anchor: والنكال: بمنزلة التنكيل، كالسلام بمعنى التسليم

SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r6.claim: الآخرة والأولى may refer to the two abodes, or to Pharaoh's two statements; on the latter view the descriptions are omitted because understood.
SAMIN-DURR:79:25/r6.anchor: والآخرة والأولى: " إما الداران، وإما الكلمتان، فالآخرة قوله

ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r1.claim: Nakāl is an accusative verbal noun used as an emphatic cognate accusative: God took him by inflicting punishment.
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r1.anchor: (نكال) منصوب مصدر مؤكد لأن معنى أخذه الله نكل به نكال الآخرة والأولى

ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r2.claim: God drowned Pharaoh in this world and will punish him in the next.
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r2.anchor: أي أغرقه في الدنيا ويعذبه في الآخرة

ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r3.claim: A tafsīr explanation takes the two terms as punishment for Pharaoh's claims that he knew no god but himself and was the highest lord.
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r3.anchor: نكال قوله: (ما علمت لكم من إله غيري). وقوله: (أنا ربكم الأعلى).

ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r1.claim: Asad clarifies that al-ula literally means the first life, here rendered as this world.

ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r2.claim: Asad points to 7:137's account of Pharaoh's destruction and its corresponding note as a parallel for the worldly punishment.
ASAD-NOTES:79:25#n11/r2.anchor: last sentence of 7:137 - "We utterly destroyed all that Pharaoh and his people had wrought, and all that they had built"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r1.claim: Putting the afterlife before this life in Pharaoh's punishment is required by the threat's meaning: its punishment is greater and more disgraceful; the same semantic emphasis explains the order in the reassurance to Muhammad.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r1.anchor: وإنما اقتضاه المعنى أولا، في سياق البشري والوعيد، إذ الآخرة خير وأبقى، وعذابها أكبر وأشد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r2.claim: Every Quranic verse ending has a contextually necessary semantic force that no substitute word could convey; its sound and verbal harmony serve that meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r2.anchor: ما من فاصلة قرآنية لا يقتضى لفظها في سياقه، دلالة معنوية لا يؤديها لفظ سواه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r3.claim: Eloquence joins meaning to its verbal delivery, rejecting fine-sounding ornament that loses or distorts meaning and forced word order chosen only for rhyme.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p278/r3.anchor: فالبلاغة من حيث هي فن القول، لا تفصل بين جوهر المعنى وبين أسلوب أدائه، ولا تعتد بمعان جليلة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses the punishment of the Hereafter as punishment for disobedience.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى ﴾ قال نكال الآخرة في المعصية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r2.claim: Qatāda says “the latter and the former” means this world and the Hereafter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ نكال الآخرة والأولى ﴾ قال الدنيا والأخرة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r3.claim: Another view takes the two terms as Pharaoh's two declarations: first his denial and disobedience and later his claim, “I am your highest lord.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#5/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم نكال الكلمتين الكلمة الأولى حين ﴿ فكذب وعصى ثم أدبر يسعى فحشر فنادى ﴾ والكلمة اللآخيرة حين قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās assigns the later punishment to Pharaoh’s claim of sole divinity and the former to his claim to be the highest lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الآخرة قوله: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r2.claim: Another view reverses Ibn ʿAbbās’s assignment of the two claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r2.anchor: وقيل العكس، وكان بين قولتيه أربعون سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r3.claim: The two boastful statements were forty years apart.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd take the later punishment as burning and the earlier one as drowning in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن زيد: نكال الآخرة بالحرق، والأولى يعني الدنيا بالغرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r5.claim: Mujāhid understands the terms as the end and beginning of Pharaoh’s life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عذاب آخرة حياته وأولاها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r6.speaker: أبو زرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r6.claim: Abū Razīn takes the first as disbelief and disobedience and the last as Pharaoh’s claim to be the highest lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r6.anchor: وقال أبو زرين: الأولى كفره وعصيانه، والآخرة قوله: أنا ربكم الأعلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r7.claim: Mujāhid also explains the pair as Pharaoh’s first and last sins, with punishment for all of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد عبارة عن أول معاصيه، وآخرها: أي نكل بالجميع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r8.claim: نكال is an absolute verbal noun governed by فأخذه because the verb carries the sense of نكّل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r8.anchor: وانتصب نكال على المصدر والعامل فيه فأخذه لأنه في معناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r9.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad instead posits an elided verb from the same root: نكّل نكال.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r9.anchor: وعلى رأي المبرد: بإضمار فعل من لفظه، أي نكل نكال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r10.claim: نكال means تنكيل, like سلام meaning تسليم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r10.anchor: والنكال بمعنى التنكيل، كالسلام بمعنى التسليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls it a confirming verbal noun, paraphrasing the sentence as God punished Pharaoh with both punishments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: نكال الآخرة هو مصدر مؤكد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r12.claim: A verbal noun confirming the prior sentence requires a governing verb inferred from that sentence’s meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r12.anchor: والمصدر المؤكد لمضمون الجملة السابقة يقدر له عامل من معنى الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r1.claim: Nakal means punitive chastisement that deters those who witness or hear of it from similar conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r1.anchor: النكال بمعنى التنكيل كالسلام بمعنى التسليم وهو التعذيب الذي ينكل من رآه أو سمعه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r2.claim: Alusi offers several parses for nakāla: emphatic verbal noun, object of the verb, purpose, object after an omitted preposition, or a circumstantial participial sense; the annexation can mean ‘in’ or ‘for’.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r2.anchor: وهو نصب على أنه مصدر مؤكد كوعد الله وصبغة الله كأنه قيل نكل الله تعالى به نكال الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r3.claim: The apparent sense is punishment in both realms: burning in the afterlife, and drowning and humiliation in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r3.anchor: وحمل الآخرة والأولى على الدارين هو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r4.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd, and others, as well as Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḍāk, and al-Shaʿbī, identify the two phrases as Pharaoh’s boasts ‘I am your supreme lord’ (later) and ‘I know no god for you but me’ (earlier).
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r4.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وابن زيد وغيرهما وعن ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك والشعبي أن الآخرة قولته أنا ربكم الأعلى والأولى قولته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r5.claim: Another view reverses which boast came first; on this account the two statements were forty years apart.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r5.anchor: وقيل بالعكس فهما كلمتان وكان بينهما على ما قالوا أربعون سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r6.speaker: أبو رزين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r6.claim: Abū Razīn takes the first as Pharaoh’s state of unbelief and rebellion, and the later as his claim to be the supreme lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r6.anchor: وقال أبو رزين الأولى حالة كفره وعصيانه والآخرة قولته أنا ربكم الأعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r7.claim: Mujāhid understands the two as Pharaoh’s earliest and latest sins, so the punishment deterred him for all his offenses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r7.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنهما عبارتان عن أول معاصيه وآخرها أي نكل بالجميع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r8.claim: On these readings, the annexation is of an effect to its cause; those who accept Pharaoh’s faith interpret the punishment as his drowning in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#5/r8.anchor: والإضافة على جميع ذلك من إضافة المسبب إلى المسبب ومآل من يقول بقبول إيمان فرعون إلى هذه الأقوال وجعل ذلك النكال الأغراق في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Pharaoh’s first and last claims as his claim to know no other god and his later claim to be supreme lord.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى} قال: بقوله: {أنا ربكم الأعلى} والأولى قوله: ما علمت

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r2.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r2.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak give the same interpretation as Ibn Abbas.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة والضحاك مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r3.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi identifies the first claim as knowing no god but himself and the last as supreme lord; forty years separated them.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الشعبي {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى} قال: هما كلمتاه الأولى

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports a forty-year interval between Pharaoh’s two statements.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: بين كلمتيه أربعون سنة

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r5.speaker: خيثمة
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r5.claim: Khaythama likewise reports forty years between Pharaoh’s two claims.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r5.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وابن المنذر عن خيثمة قال: كان بين قول فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r1.claim: Nakālan is a cognate accusative specifying the kind of taking, since taking can occur in many forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r1.anchor: وانتصب نكال } على المفعولية المطلقة لفعل ( أخذه ) مبين لنوع الأخذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r2.claim: The genitive construction with the Hereafter and first life means ‘in’.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r2.anchor: وإضافة { نكال } إلى { الآخرة والأولى } على معنى ( في ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r3.claim: The first-life chastisement was drowning; the Hereafter’s punishment is Hellfire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r3.anchor: فالنكال في الأولى هو الغرق ، والنكال في الآخرة هو عذاب جهنم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r4.claim: The term nakāl is literal for what befell Pharaoh in this world.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r4.anchor: ما حصل لفرعون في الدنيا هو نكال حقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r5.claim: For the Hereafter, nakāl is figurative: Hell’s severe torment resembles chastisement, though it cannot deter anyone on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r5.anchor: وما يصيبه في الآخرة أطلق عليه النكال لأنه يشبه النكال في شدة التعذيب ولا يحصل به نكال يوم القيامة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r6.claim: The past tense treats future punishment as begun: after death Pharaoh starts tasting it and seeing his eventual destination, as a hadith relates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r6.anchor: مراعى فيه أنه لما مات ابتدأ يذوق العذاب حين يرى منزلته التي سيؤول إليها يوم الجزاء كما ورد في الحديث .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r7.claim: The Hereafter is named before the first life because its matter is greater.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r7.anchor: وتقديم { الآخرة } على { الأولى } في الذكر لأن أمر الآخرة أعظم .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والشعبي ومقاتل والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r1.claim: The first saying was Pharaoh's claim that he knew no god besides himself, and the later one was his claim to be the highest lord; Ibn ʿAbbās says forty years separated them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r1.anchor: أحدها أن الاولى قوله ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r2.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Najīḥ transmits from Mujāhid the same identification of the first and later sayings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r2.anchor: ورواه ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says forty years passed between Pharaoh's two claims.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وكان بينهما أربعون سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh lived thirty years after making the later claim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r4.anchor: قال السدي فبقي بعد الآخرة ثلاثين سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ paraphrases the verse as God taking him as a deterrent for both his later and earlier claims.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r5.anchor: قال الفراء فالمعنى أخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r6.claim: A second view takes the phrase to mean God made Pharaoh a deterrent in this world and the next, drowning him here and punishing him in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r6.anchor: والثاني المعنى جعله الله نكال الدنيا والآخرة أغرقه في الدنيا وعذبه في الآخرة قاله الحسن وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says Pharaoh was punished by drowning at the day's beginning and fire at its end.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس عذبه الله في أول النهار بالغرق وفي آخرة بالنار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r8.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r8.claim: A third view makes the first refer to Pharaoh's denial and disobedience, and the later one to his claim to be the highest lord.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r9.speaker: منصور عن مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r9.claim: A fourth view, transmitted by Manṣūr from Mujāhid, takes the words as Pharaoh's first and last deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r9.anchor: والرابع أنها اول أعماله وآخرها رواه منصور عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj says nakālan is an accusative cognate verbal noun, because the sense is that God punished him as a deterrent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#5/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج النكال منصوب مصدر مؤكد لأن معنى أخذه الله نكل الله به نكال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r17.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r17.claim: The punishment covers this world and the next: drowning in this life and fire in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r17.anchor: عقوبة الدنيا والآخرة , قال قتادة : عذبه الله في الدنيا بالغرق وفي الآخرة بالنار

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r18.claim: The phrase can mean punishment at the beginning and end of Pharaoh’s life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r18.anchor: عذاب أول عمره وآخره , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r19.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r19.claim: Ikrima identifies the earlier claim as I am unaware of any god for you but me, and the later one as I am your highest lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r19.anchor: الأولى قوله : ( ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ) والآخرة قوله ( أنا ربكم الأعلى ) , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r20.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two claims were forty years apart, while Mujahid and al-Suddi give thirty years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r20.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وكان بينهما أربعون سنة , وقال مجاهد : ثلاثون سنة , قال السدي : وهي الآخرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r21.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r21.claim: The first punishment was respite, and the last was Hell, as described in 40:46.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r21.anchor: النار يعرضون عليها } الآية , قاله الربيع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r1.claim: Nakal means making an example of someone, as salām means giving peace.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r1.anchor: والنكال بمعنى التنكيل كالسلام بمعنى التسليم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r2.claim: The accusative is a cognate accusative because “seizing” here has the sense of “punishing”: God punished him with a punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r2.anchor: ونصبه على المصدر لأن أخذ بمعنى نكل كأنه قيل نكل الله به نكال الأخرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r3.claim: One explanation takes the punishment as burning, the punishment of the Hereafter, and the earlier punishment as drowning.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, the punishment answers Pharaoh's two claims: “I am your highest lord” and “I know no god for you but me”; Nasafi gives forty, thirty, or twenty years between them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#3/r4.anchor: أو نكال كلمتيه الآخرة وهى أنا ربكم الأعلى والأولى

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r1.claim: Pharaoh's punishment in both the afterlife and worldly life is the fate of tyrants.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r1.anchor: وذلك هو مصير الطغاة في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p251/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r1.claim: The deterrent aspect of punishment operates in this world: hearing about afterlife punishment restrains people from actions that lead to it.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r1.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يصور في الآخرة بل في الدنيا فإن العقوبة الأخروية تنكل من سمعها وتمنعه من تعاطي ما يؤدي إليها

BURSEVI:v10p251/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r2.speaker: التأويلات القاشانية
BURSEVI:v10p251/r2.claim: The Qashānī inward reading sees Pharaoh contesting the Real through manifest selfhood clothed in pride; God subdued and cast him into Hell, as in the saying that pride is God’s mantle.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r2.anchor: نازع الحق بشدة ظهور أنانيته في رداء الكبرياء فقهر وقذف في النار ملعونا

BURSEVI:v10p251/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r3.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v10p251/r3.claim: Al-Baqlī says Pharaoh’s false claim disgraced him in both worlds, as happens to anyone claiming spiritual stations they do not possess.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r3.anchor: افتضح في الدنيا والآخرة وهكذا كل ما يدعي ما ليس له من المقامات

BURSEVI:v10p251/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r4.speaker: بشر
BURSEVI:v10p251/r4.claim: Bishr says God let Pharaoh’s tongue utter grand claims while emptying them of their realities.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r4.anchor: قال بشر انطق الله لسانه بالعريض من الدعاوي وإخلاء عن حقائقها

BURSEVI:v10p251/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r5.speaker: السري
BURSEVI:v10p251/r5.claim: Al-Sarī says a servant who dresses as a master becomes a warning; Pharaoh’s claim to lordship was refuted by everything, even himself.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r5.anchor: العبد إذا تزيى بزي السيد صار نكالا ألا ترى كيف ذكر الله

BURSEVI:v10p251/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r6.speaker: موسى
BURSEVI:v10p251/r6.claim: A report in al-Wasīṭ says Moses asked why Pharaoh was spared for 400 years while claiming divinity and resisting the messengers; God replied that Pharaoh was good-natured and easy to approach, so He repaid him in this world.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r6.anchor: وفي الوسيط عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال موسى

BURSEVI:v10p251/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r7.claim: The report explains the worldly recompense for a disbeliever’s good deeds, whereas a believer receives most of their reward in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r7.anchor: فأردت إن أكافئه أي مكافأة دنيوية وكذا حسنات كل كافر وإما المؤمن فأكثر ثوابه في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p251/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r8.claim: The account indicates that Pharaoh died an unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r8.anchor: ودلت الآية على أن فرعون مات كافرا

BURSEVI:v10p251/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r9.speaker: الفتوحات المكية
BURSEVI:v10p251/r9.claim: The Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya says Pharaoh and Nimrod remain in Hell eternally.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r9.anchor: فرعون ونمرود مؤبدان في النار انتهى

BURSEVI:v10p251/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r10.claim: Bursevi treats the Shaykh’s other statements as dialectical discussion and warns against prolonged debate, which he calls severe misguidance.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r10.anchor: محمول على المباحثة فصن لسانك عن الإطالة فإنها من أشد ضلالة

BURSEVI:v10p251/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r11.claim: Bursevi notes that Pharaoh’s two claims, forty years apart, make it likely that highest lordship meant divinity; reading it merely as political supremacy proves little, since rulers and materialists need not claim divinity.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r11.anchor: صدر من فرعون كلمتان الأولى قوله أنا ربكم الأعلى والثانية قوله ما عملت لكم من إله غيري وبينهما على ما قيل أربعون سنة

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.claim: Pharaoh's punishment answered his later claim “I am your highest lord” and his earlier claim “I know no god for you but myself.”
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.claim: Abū Bakr says the two boasts were forty years apart, attributing the account to Ibn ʿAbbās through Abū Ḥuṣayn and Abū al-Ḍuḥā.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر، وسئل عن هذا، فقال: كان بينهما أربعون سنة

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the first boast as Pharaoh's claim to be the only god and the later one as his claim to be the highest lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the two boasts and reports a forty-year interval between them.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī gives the same identification of Pharaoh's two boasts as retribution for the first and later claims.

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.claim: ʿĀmir likewise identifies the two boasts as Pharaoh's claims to divinity and to being the highest lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.anchor: عن زكريا، عن عامر، {نكال الآخرة والأولى}

THALABI:v10p127/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r5.claim: God seized Pharaoh and punished him in this world by drowning and in the next by fire.
THALABI:v10p127/r5.anchor: فأخذه الله فعاقبه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى يعني في الدنيا والآخرة

THALABI:v10p127/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p127/r6.claim: An alternative takes the first and last as Pharaoh's two statements, “I know no god for you but myself” and “I am your highest lord,” separated by forty years.
